regulations.title: AGLC liquor licence required to manufacture alcohol (Class E or Class F)
regulations.summary: Any business that distills, brews, or makes wine/cider in Alberta needs a liquor licence from Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) before producing anything for sale - Class E covers distilleries, wineries and meaderies, and Class F covers breweries and ferment-on-premises brewing.
regulations.regulation_name: Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act and Regulation
regulations.action_required: Apply for the correct AGLC manufacturer licence class (E for spirits/wine/mead, F for beer) through AGLC's Online Licensing Portal, including criminal record checks for directors and shareholders.
regulations.penalty_note: Manufacturing or selling liquor without the required AGLC licence is an offence under the Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act, subject to fines and product seizure.
regulations.source_name: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC) - Licensing

regulations.title: Sales must flow through Alberta's privatized wholesale/retail liquor system
regulations.summary: Unlike Ontario, Quebec, or BC, Alberta has no government-run liquor stores or warehouses. AGLC is the legal importer of record, but all warehousing, distribution, and retailing is done by privately licensed businesses, so to get your product on shelves it needs to be carried by AGLC-licensed private wholesalers and retailers (like Class D liquor stores).
regulations.regulation_name: Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act and Regulation - Alberta's liquor model
regulations.action_required: Arrange for your registered products to be carried by AGLC-licensed private retailers/wholesalers (e.g., Class D liquor stores); there is no government retail channel to sell through in Alberta.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling liquor outside AGLC's licensed private retail/wholesale system is prohibited and can trigger enforcement action against both the seller and the retailer.

regulations.title: Out-of-province producers need a registered Alberta liquor agency to represent them
regulations.summary: If you make alcohol outside Alberta and want to sell it here, you can't just ship it in directly - you need a registered liquor agency (or your own AGLC-registered agency) to import, list, and market your product with AGLC on your behalf.
regulations.regulation_name: Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act and Regulation - liquor agency registration
regulations.action_required: Appoint an AGLC-registered liquor agency (or register your own) and obtain a valid Liquor Agency (LA) number before listing products for sale in Alberta.
regulations.penalty_note: Products without registered agency representation cannot be listed or sold through AGLC's system.

regulations.title: Liquor markup applied to every product sold through AGLC
regulations.summary: Alberta doesn't have a separate sales tax on alcohol - instead, AGLC applies a per-litre markup (which varies by beverage type and alcohol content) on every product sold, and that markup is what funds the province's liquor-related revenue.
regulations.regulation_name: Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Act - liquor markup rate schedule
regulations.action_required: Review AGLC's current liquor markup rate schedule for your product category and build it into your wholesale pricing before listing products for sale.
regulations.penalty_note: Markup is collected by AGLC as part of the wholesale transaction; mispricing or attempting to bypass it can result in listing suspension.

regulations.title: Beverage container registration and deposit for beer, wine, spirits, and cooler containers
regulations.summary: Every beer, wine, spirits, or cooler container sold in Alberta must be registered with the province's beverage container recycling program, with a refundable deposit and recycling fee collected on each unit.
regulations.authority: Beverage Container Management Board (BCMB) / Alberta Beverage Container Recycling Corporation (ABCRC)
regulations.action_required: Register your company and container types with ABCRC/BCMB, pay the initial deposit, and remit the per-container deposit and recycling fee on every unit sold.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling unregistered beverage containers violates the Beverage Container Recycling Regulation and can lead to removal from sale and financial penalties.
